name: Alfa Romeo 1900 C52 "Disco Volante"
description:
The Disco Volante — flying saucer — was Alfa Romeo's attempt to find out how much a body shape was worth. Touring of Milan built three of them in 1952 on a shortened 1900 chassis, in their Superleggera way: a light alloy skin over a cage of small-diameter tubes, with the flanks drawn out into a full-width ellipse that gave the car its name and made it look, from above, like nothing else on a starting grid.

The first cars had a two-litre twin-cam four of 158 hp in a 735 kg car and were timed at over 220 km/h. A three-litre straight-six version followed. None of them ever raced seriously — Alfa was withdrawing from competition as the project matured, and the Disco Volante ended as a rolling wind-tunnel study whose lessons went into the road cars instead.
author: Irgam
